messages:
maria: Hey folks — PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8345 is red in CI because of a flaky test `test_cache_eviction`. It passes locally. Can someone take a quick look? failing job: https://ci.redwood.com/builds/11902 :pray:
ci-bot: build 11902 failed on ubuntu-latest (integration). Failing step: pytest tests/integration/test_cache.py::test_cache_eviction. Full logs: https://ci.redwood.com/builds/11902/logs
eli: I can check in ~15m. Do you have the failure log snippet?
maria: here's the tail of the failing log:
```
E       AssertionError: expected eviction count 3 got 2
/opt/runner/work/redwood/tests/integration/test_cache.py:87: AssertionError
```
It timed out waiting for eviction in the CI worker.
sam: could be a timing issue on slow runners. Might be the eviction background thread runs less frequently on CI. @kyle any idea?
kyle: looking now. Test assumes eviction tick ~200ms; CI runners sometimes run at ~500ms under load. We should either bump the wait in the test or mock the timer. I'll try a tiny test patch.
jen: if we need a quick unblock, can we rerun the job? also consider marking as flaky in flaky-tests.json if intermittent :thinking_face:
maria: rerun queued -> https://ci.redwood.com/builds/11903
ci-bot: re-run 11903 started (triggered by @maria).
kyle: pushed a small change to use eventual_assert(timeout=2.0) in the test. Commented on the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8345#issuecomment-0000000. Waiting for rerun result.
ci-bot: build 11903 succeeded.
eli: nice, looks stable on rerun. I think the eventual_assert is fine. We should open a ticket to make eviction deterministic for tests.
jen: opened issue #2710: "Make cache eviction deterministic in tests" and linked the PR.
maria: thanks @kyle and @eli for the quick help — I'll merge once green and update changelog.
kyle: cool, happy to help :thumbsup:
